n38ab075470d.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the broad periods of the Chalukya branches?
o: Kalyani was the earliest of the three branches
n38ab075470d.x: The order is Badami (6th–8th c.), Vengi (7th–11th c.) and Kalyani (late 10th–12th c.), so Kalyani was the latest, not the earliest.

n9c9a57f804a.s: In the Imperial Chola succession, who ruled immediately after the founder Vijayalaya?
n9c9a57f804a.x: The succession runs Vijayalaya, Aditya I, Rajaraja I and Rajendra I; Aditya I followed the founder.

n8cafb30bfd3.s: Under the 73rd Amendment, the intermediate tier of Panchayats may be omitted in a State whose population does not exceed:
n8cafb30bfd3.x: The intermediate tier is optional in a State with a population not exceeding twenty lakh.

n0db289e952b.s: Which of the following was a qualification for membership of a Chola village committee?
n0db289e952b.x: Owning a residence was a qualification, whereas failure to submit accounts, committing sins and stealing property were disqualifications.

new.s: Kalyani, the capital of the Western Chalukyas, is the present-day:
new.x: Kalyani is present Basavakalyan in Karnataka; Badami was the earlier Chalukya capital.

new.s: Which Kalyani Chalukya ruler took the title 'Vengi Purveshwara' after the battle of Koppam?
new.x: Someshvara I Ahavamalla took the title Vengi Purveshwara after killing Rajadhiraja I at Koppam (1053).

new.s: Which Kalyani Chalukya ruler sent Bayyalanambi against Vengi in 1006 CE?
new.x: Satyasraya sent Bayyalanambi against Vengi in 1006; he was repulsed by Saktivarman I with Chola help.

new.s: The Chalukya-Vikrama era started in:
new.x: Vikramaditya VI founded the era in 1076 CE, the year of his accession; 973 CE is Tailapa II's overthrow of the Rashtrakutas.

new.s: The principal cause of the wars between the Kalyani Chalukyas and the Cholas was rivalry over:
new.x: The Chola-Chalukya wars were fought mainly over Vengi (coastal Andhra) and the Raichur doab.

new.s: The battle of Kudalasangamam (c. 1062) was fought at the confluence of:
new.x: Kudalasangamam lies at the Krishna–Tungabhadra confluence, where the Cholas heavily defeated Someshvara I.

new.s: Which Chola king was killed by Someshvara I at the battle of Koppam (1053)?
new.x: Someshvara I killed Rajadhiraja I at Koppam; Rajendra II succeeded him.

new.s: Bilhana, the author of Vikramankadevacharita, came from:
new.x: Bilhana was a Kashmiri poet at the court of Vikramaditya VI.

new.s: In Vikramankadevacharita, Bilhana likens the reign of Vikramaditya VI to:
new.x: Bilhana's biography of Vikramaditya VI likens his reign to Ramarajya.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Manasollasa:
1. It is a 100-chapter encyclopaedia.
2. Its subjects include agriculture, medicine and cuisine.
3. It was written by Vikramaditya VI.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The Manasollasa is a 100-chapter encyclopaedia covering statecraft, agriculture, medicine, music and cuisine; it was written by Someshvara III, not Vikramaditya VI.

new.s: The Manasollasa was written by:
new.x: Someshvara III (1126–1138) wrote the Manasollasa.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Mitakshara?
o: It is a commentary on the Yajnavalkya Smriti
Under it sons acquire a right in ancestral property by birth
It applied only to the upper castes
new.x: The claim that Mitakshara was for upper castes and Dayabhaga for lower castes is wrong; the other three statements are correct.

new.s: The Dayabhaga school of inheritance prevails in:
new.x: Dayabhaga, by Jimutavahana, prevails in Bengal and Assam; the Mitakshara covers most of India.

new.s: The legal work Daan Sagar was written by:
new.x: Daan Sagar was written by Ballal Sena; Devana Bhatta wrote Smriti Chandrika.

new.s: The Kasivishveshvara temple of the Kalyani Chalukya period is at:
new.x: The Kasivishveshvara temple is at Lakkundi; Itagi has the Mahadeva temple and Dambal the Doddabasappa temple.

new.s: The star-shaped (stellate) temple plans of the Kalyani Chalukyas later became a model for the:
new.x: The stellate plans of the Gadag style were later taken up as a model by the Hoysalas.

new.s: The Hoysalas, a successor power of the Kalyani Chalukyas, ruled from:
new.x: The Hoysala capital was Dwarasamudra; the Yadavas ruled from Devagiri.

new.s: Which of the following pairs of successor powers and capitals is correctly matched?
new.x: The Kakatiyas ruled from Hanamkonda–Warangal; the Hoysalas ruled from Dwarasamudra, the Yadavas from Devagiri and the Kalachuris from Kalyani.

new.s: Before founding the imperial line, Vijayalaya was a feudatory of the Pallavas at:
new.x: Vijayalaya was a Pallava feudatory at Uraiyur and captured Thanjavur from the Muttaraiyars in 850 CE.

new.s: Vijayalaya captured Thanjavur in 850 CE from the:
new.x: Vijayalaya took Thanjavur from the Muttaraiyars in 850 CE and founded the imperial Chola line.

new.s: Who was the last ruler of the Imperial Chola dynasty?
new.x: Rajendra III (1246–1279) was the last Imperial Chola; the Pandyas rose after him.

new.s: Which Chola ruler was crowned on the battlefield of Koppam?
new.x: Rajendra II was crowned on the field at Koppam after Rajadhiraja I was killed; he set up a victory pillar at Kolhapur.

new.s: The title 'Madurai-konda' belonged to:
new.x: Parantaka I took the title Madurai-konda after capturing Madurai from the Pandyas.

new.s: The title 'Pandita Chola' was borne by:
new.x: Rajendra I was called Pandita Chola as a patron of learning; he was also Gangaikonda Chola and Kadaram Kondan.

new.s: The title 'Yanai-mel-thunjina Devar' refers to the Chola king who:
o: Died on an elephant at Koppam
new.x: Rajadhiraja I was called Yanai-mel-thunjina Devar because he died on an elephant at Koppam.

new.s: Northern Sri Lanka, named 'Mummadichola Mandalam', is linked with the title Mummudi Chola of:
new.x: Rajaraja I took the title Mummudi Chola; northern Sri Lanka was named Mummadichola Mandalam.

new.s: Rajaraja I destroyed the Chera navy at:
new.x: Rajaraja I destroyed the Chera fleet at Kandalur Salai (Trivandrum) and captured Quilon.

new.s: Which Chola ruler conquered the Maldives islands?
new.x: Rajaraja I's naval conquests included the Maldives, the Chera fleet and northern Sri Lanka.

new.s: Jayamkondar's Kalingattuparani celebrates the Kalinga conquest of:
new.x: Kulottunga I conquered Kalinga, a campaign sung in Jayamkondar's Kalingattuparani.

new.s: Gangaikondacholapuram was founded as the new Chola capital around:
new.x: Rajendra I founded Gangaikondacholapuram c. 1035 CE; 1010 is the completion of the Brihadeeswara temple.

new.s: According to the APPSC Group 2 (2008) key, Rajahmundry (Rajamahendravaram) was built by:
new.x: Amma I made Rajamahendravaram the capital, but Rajaraja Narendra made it famous and is credited with building it.

new.s: In the battle of Takkolam (949 CE), Parantaka I was defeated by:
new.x: Takkolam was a Chola defeat: the Rashtrakuta Krishna III beat Parantaka I.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Chola battles:
1. The Cholas won the battle of Takkolam.
2. Rajendra II was crowned on the battlefield of Koppam.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Rajendra II was crowned at Koppam after Rajadhiraja I died; Takkolam (949) was won by the Rashtrakutas.

new.s: After the Chola victory at Kalidindi, who built three Shiva temples for the fallen Chola commanders?
new.x: Rajaraja Narendra built three Shiva temples for the Chola commanders who fell at Kalidindi.

new.s: Madhurantaki, wife of Kulottunga I, was the daughter of:
new.x: Madhurantaki was the daughter of Rajendra II and married Rajendra Chalukya (Kulottunga I).

new.s: The Chola viceroy Rajaraja (Mummadi Chola), son of Kulottunga I, installed whom in Kalinga?
new.x: Rajaraja (Mummadi Chola) installed Anantavarman Chodaganga in Kalinga; Gonka I was his commander.

new.s: The Chola viceroy Rajaraja Chola Ganga was crowned at Jananathapura, identified with:
new.x: Rajaraja Chola Ganga was crowned at Jananathapura (Draksharama); his Tekkali inscription records his rule.

new.s: Who was the last Eastern Chalukya ruler of Vengi?
new.x: Vijayaditya VII was the last Eastern Chalukya; Parantaka Chola was the last Chalukya-Chola ruler in Vengi.

new.s: Kulottunga I sent 72 merchants to China in the year:
new.x: Kulottunga I sent a goodwill mission of 72 merchants to China in 1077.

new.s: Kulottunga I married his daughter to the Sinhala prince:
new.x: Kulottunga I gave Sri Lanka its freedom and married his daughter to the Sinhala prince Virapperumal.

new.s: Which South Indian dynasty's sabha and ur assemblies formed the base on which the Cholas built their local self-government?
new.x: Sabha and ur assemblies already appear under the Pallavas; the Badami Chalukyas were highly centralised.

new.s: The nattar, the assembly of the Chola nadu, was made up mainly of leading:
new.x: The nattar consisted of leading vellala (peasant) landholders; merchants formed the nagaram.

new.s: In Chola administration, the nadu was:
new.x: The ur was the village and the nadu a group of villages, whose assembly was the nattar.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Chola nattar:
1. It handled revenue collection and disputes above the village level.
2. It was a body created under the 73rd Amendment.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The nattar handled revenue and disputes above village level; it was a Chola body, not a 73rd Amendment body.

new.s: The Chola sabha (mahasabha) functioned in:
new.x: The sabha met in brahmadeya (rent-free agrahara) villages and had Brahmans only; the ur was in non-brahmadeya villages.

new.s: Membership of the Chola sabha was confined to:
new.x: The sabha of brahmadeya villages consisted of Brahmans only; merchants formed the nagaram.

new.s: The Uttaramerur inscriptions are located in which district of Tamil Nadu?
new.x: Uttaramerur is in Kanchipuram district; its inscriptions are dated 919 and 921 CE under Parantaka I.

new.s: Under the Uttaramerur rules, a candidate for a village committee had to be aged:
new.x: The age qualification was 35 to 70 years, along with land, a house and Vedic learning.

new.s: Under the kudavolai system, the village was divided into how many wards (kudumbus)?
new.x: The village was split into 30 wards (kudumbus) for the lottery.

new.s: Members chosen by kudavolai for a Chola village committee served a term of:
new.x: Committee members served 360 days; those who had served in the past three years were barred.

new.s: In the kudavolai procedure, the names were drawn from the pot by:
new.x: A young boy or girl drew the palm-leaf names from the pot by lot.

new.s: In Chola village administration, 'perumakkal' meant:
new.x: Perumakkal were the members of the village assembly; kudumbu was the ward and kudavolai the lottery.

new.s: Which of the following pairs of Chola terms is correctly matched?
new.x: Variyam meant committee; kudumbu was the ward, kudavolai the lottery and perumakkal the assembly members.

new.s: The eri variyam of a Chola village looked after:
new.x: The eri variyam managed tanks and the distribution of water to fields.

new.s: The pon variyam of a Chola village dealt with:
new.x: Pon means gold: the pon variyam handled finance and checked currency.

new.s: The panchavara variyam in Chola villages was the:
new.x: The panchavara variyam was the standing (supervisory) committee; the samvatsara variyam was the annual committee.

new.s: Which of the following was a power of Chola village assemblies?
o: Auctioning the land of tax defaulters
new.x: Assemblies levied taxes, raised loans and auctioned defaulters' land; they were absolute proprietors of village lands.

new.s: Unlike the 73rd Amendment, Chola village assemblies had:
new.x: Chola assemblies had no women's quota, whereas Article 243D reserves at least one-third of seats for women.

new.s: Which historian described the Chola state as a 'segmentary state'?
new.x: Burton Stein called it a segmentary state where local autonomy stayed intact at the periphery; Nilakanta Sastri spoke of grassroots democracy.
